cells.tense: You are seeing it clearly right now, and you are not standing in the way of it.
cells.ask: Say out loud what you notice in one thing that's growing, then go back to tending it and add nothing. Let the sentence stand where you left it.
cells.core:
You're noticing what's actually there in the thing you're tending — not what you hope is there, not what it was last month. Early sight, before it has a name. And you're not standing in the way of it. You water, you wait, you let it be smaller than it will be.

That's rarer than it sounds. Most people who look that closely start steering. You look and you let it grow on its own schedule. You and what you're growing are moving at the same speed right now, and the thing in front of you is getting both your eye and your patience. Whatever you're tending gets to keep its own pace. Keep your hand open like this and it will keep showing you what it is.
cells.sheetLine: You see it clearly and you let it grow at its own pace.
cells.verb: seeing what's there before there's anything to name yet
cells.place: in the garden where something is still small enough to need tending

cells.tense: You are already watching something that hasn't happened yet, and you are watching it hard.
cells.ask: Pick one growing thing and leave it unwatched for a full day. Don't check on it, don't plan for it, don't run ahead of it in your head.
cells.core:
You're ahead of something again — watching a thing that hasn't happened, checking it before it's grown enough to check. The clarity you've got is real, but it's aimed at a version of this that doesn't exist yet, and it's spending itself on a shape you drew in advance.

Meanwhile the thing right in front of you is smaller than your idea of it, which is what growing things are. You can look at it as it is today, or you can keep standing over a future it can't catch you in. One of those is care. The other is you, braced. Set the watch down for a day and see what's actually there when you come back.
cells.sheetLine: You're watching a future that hasn't arrived and missing what's here.
cells.verb: seeing what's there before there's anything to name yet
cells.place: in the garden where something is still small enough to need tending

cells.tense: You stopped looking at it closely a while back, and you kept going through the motions of tending.
cells.ask: Look hard at one thing you tend, today, with no fixing in mind. Write down one thing you see, then go do something you chose on your own.
cells.core:
You're tending something and not really looking at it anymore. The work still happens — you water, you show up — but the close look stopped, and without it the care is going through the motions. The hands are still moving. The attention isn't.

When it's going well, this is quiet work: you know the difference between a plant that's resting and one that's struggling, and you act on what you see without making a project of it. That's what's not running now. What won't come back by trying is the attention itself, and pushing yourself to feel more won't get it there either. Pick up one thing of your own — something you've been meaning to finish — and finish it. That's the channel that opens this. Then look at what you're growing again, and see what's actually there.
cells.sheetLine: You still do the work, but you've stopped looking at what you're growing.
cells.verb: seeing what's there before there's anything to name yet
cells.place: in the garden where something is still small enough to need tending

cells.tense: You are already seeing what's growing accurately, and you talk about it as if it were nothing special.
cells.ask: Tell one person the plain thing you noticed in what you're tending, and don't add the part where anyone could have seen it.
cells.core:
You're already looking at what you're growing and getting it right — reading the small signs, knowing when to water, when to wait, when something's finished. You do this all day. You'd call it just paying attention, or the obvious thing to do.

What you do with your eyes is yours. Nobody handed it to you, and it isn't the kind of thing you get to shrug off as ordinary. When you say what you saw, say it as yours — the read you made, not the read that was lying around. It changes nothing about what you do. It changes who's holding it, and that's the part that's been missing.
cells.sheetLine: You see it right and you call it nothing. The read is yours.
